interpretations.rationale: The executed receipts establish a decided-index invariant violation and the follower stall it produces. Receipt b4129a8c87e844c4832499bc34b21bdd ran randomized_reconfig_diagnose_lag (exit 0, test passed). Its event 1 reports decided 38,38,37,38,38 after 150 fair-delivery rounds; both declared comparisons are complete and violated, the convergence comparison because the nodes do not agree, and the invariant comparison because p4_gap, node 4's decided index minus its accepted index, is 1. The same event records node 3 at accepted 37 and decided 37 with is_reconfigured Some, node 4 at accepted 37 and decided 38 with is_reconfigured None, and identical entry kinds on both nodes at indices 35, 36 and 37: a decided value, a StopSign, and nothing. The two logs therefore agree at the reconfiguration position, and leader 4 did not lose the StopSign entry; what it lost is the cached marker, which sync_log clears when a later LogSync carries stopsign None while leaving the appended entry in place. The leader's decided index of 38 has no matching entry in its own log and exceeds its own accepted index, which handle_accepted permits by setting the decided index from a follower-reported accepted index once is_chosen counts a quorum, without comparing it to the leader's accepted index. Node 3's inbound trace, prepare:0-0>0-0|prepare:0-0>0-0|prepare:0-0>0-0|promise:0-0>0-0|promise:0-0>0-0|promise:0-0>0-0|accsync1:0-0>37-0|decide2:37-0>37-37|decide3:37-37>37-37, shows the AcceptSync raising it to accepted 37 and the two Decides, the immediate successors of that sync's sequence counter, being accepted as expected messages and clamped to decided 37. Node 3 sends no PrepareReq, so no reconnection follows; it already accepted a StopSign, so the periodic path offers no AcceptStopSign; and repeated Decides reuse a consumed sequence number, so they are ignored. The follower therefore stays one index behind for the whole window. The zero divergence figure is not evidence of agreement: the harness keeps only Decided(Value) entries and compares the shorter prefix, so StopSign entries and prefix lengths are never compared.
counterevidence: A follower that genuinely missed the AcceptStopSign can still recover: in the constructed clean-miss run the periodic Decide was sequence-ahead, the follower reconnected, and an AcceptSync repaired it.
A leadership change, or an external reconnected() call, leads to Prepare/Promise/AcceptSync, which gives the follower a fresh sequence and a log sync from the new leader.
The two logs agree at indices 35 to 37, so this is not a value or marker divergence between node 3 and leader 4 at those positions.
The invariant violation is on the leader, not on the stalled follower: node 3's decided equals its accepted index, while node 4's decided exceeds its accepted index by one.
limitations: Entry kinds, is_reconfigured and the index gap are sampled once at the end, so the receipt does not show when the marker was cleared or when the decided index passed the local log.
Node 3's inbound trace is capped at twelve messages after the lossy phase, and Promises to node 4 are recorded only when delivered and only up to forty entries.
The divergence check keeps only Decided(Value) entries and compares the shorter prefix, so it cannot detect a StopSign-versus-value disagreement or a length difference.
Five nodes, MemoryStorage, unit batch, no snapshots and no next configuration started; flexible quorums, batching and snapshot-based sync are unexercised.
